title: Finite, integral and rational cyclic sheet equivalences
statement: Fix the finite-field datum D, m$\ge$1, separated finite-type X_0, a coefficient prime l$\ne$p, and G : ZlSheetGeometry D m hm X_0 as in [def-zl-constant-extension-sheet-heart-data]. The actual canonical sheet maps satisfy ZlSheetCoefficientClauses D m hm X_0 l hl: finite, integral and rational product equivalences detecting both standard halves with exact full-heart restrictions; cohomology, coefficient reductions and quotient comparisons; and normalized integral and rational scalar-extension comparisons for all finite coefficient fields. No common-stage or Weil-coordinate conclusion is asserted.

proof.text: For each coordinate isomorphism $r_i:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y_i$ and for $g_X$, use [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]: reindexing on the pro-etale sites gives exact inverse equivalences on constant-coefficient module sheaves. By [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] the actual finite and integral pullbacks are the termwise inverse-image functors with the specified coefficient action. The finite constructible categories are preserved by that lemma, for both the isomorphism and its inverse. At integral, rational and common-field stages [lem-pod-isomorphism-field-transport] supplies the actual inverse equivalences and their scalar-compatible inverse identities. Termwise exact inverse image commutes with kernels and images, hence with cohomology. It preserves both integral standard halves; the rational and common-field halves are isomorphism closures of the preceding halves by [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], so both inverse functors preserve those halves too. They therefore restrict to equivalences of standard hearts; these are exact since kernels and cokernels are preserved by an additive equivalence of abelian categories.

source.place: Functoriality of the pro-etale site; isomorphism reindexing, followed by the prescribed integral and field coefficient constructions

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] to $Y=\coprod_iY_i$ and compose its restriction equivalence with the coordinate equivalences of Step 3. Since $h_i=j_i\circ r_i$, the composition isomorphism $L(j_ir_i)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lr_i^*Lj_i^*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] at finite level and of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] at integral level, rationalized and passed to common stages by the morphism rules of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], identifies this composite naturally with $R:N\mapsto(h_i^*N)_i$; a functor naturally isomorphic to an equivalence is an equivalence. A quasi-inverse first transports $A_i$ to $Y_i$ by the inverse of $r_i^*$, then glues by the finite clopen quasi-inverse. Componentwise cohomology in the cited lemma and Step 3 show that $R$ and its inverse preserve the standard halves and restrict to exact heart equivalences. The same lemma gives compatibility with reduction and scalar extension for clopen restriction, and Step 3 gives it for each coordinate isomorphism. Their composites give that compatibility for $R$ and its inverse. Thus every coefficient stage in the statement is covered. An individual $h_i^*$ is an exact projection after this equivalence; its coordinate factor $r_i^*$, rather than this projection from all of $Y$, is the equivalence.

proof.text: The compositors used above are the specified ones, not arbitrary choices: [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] prescribes all finite reductions and the associativity identity, so the repeated comparison $(g_X^m)^*\simeq P^m$ is coherent. Part 1 of [lem-pod-pullback-identities-scalar-extension] says that extending a compositor and then applying the two scalar comparisons equals applying the scalar comparison for the composite and then the new compositor. Thus every $\tau_i$, including the iterated return, commutes with finite coefficient extension. Rationalization sends the same integral comparisons to rational arrows; in the actual common-stage category of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], arrows are their classes over a common finite field. The preceding equality makes the two induced common-stage arrows equal after any further extension. Hence the coordinate constructions and equations retain exactly the integral normalization required by [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category].
